_comment: Expected state of every upstream pin that xtcp2 depends on for its netlink
tooling, recorded so that drift is visible rather than silent.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. proto-audit — the netlink layout oracle wired up in
nix/checks/proto-audit-netlink.nix — reaches xtcp2 through TWO pins, and
both can go stale independently:
1. xtcp2's own `xdp2` flake input. If xdp2's main moves, we keep
auditing against an older oracle: new NL_* protocols it has learned
about, and fixes to its extractors, never reach us.
2. xdp2's OWN pin of xtcp2 (`xtcp2Rev` in its
nix/proto-audit-sources.nix). This is the one that bites, because it
is proto-audit's DEFAULT for --xtcp2-src. Left at the default, the
oracle audits a GitHub snapshot of xtcp2 from over a year ago and
reports findings about code nobody is running. The oracle check
overrides it to this tree and asserts the override took — see
`stale_note` below for exactly how stale it is.
HOW THIS FILE IS CHECKED. Two halves, because a `nix flake check` sandbox
has no network and so physically cannot ask GitHub whether main has moved:
- nix/checks/upstream-pins.nix (hermetic, in `nix flake check`) asserts
the revs below still match flake.lock and xdp2's own source. It catches
a pin CHANGING without this file being updated.
- `nix run .#check-upstream-pins` (needs network) asks the remotes where
main actually is and reports drift. It catches upstream MOVING. Warns
by default; --strict exits non-zero for CI.
Refresh `rev` here whenever you move a pin, and re-measure the drift
numbers with the runner rather than editing them by recollection.

xdp2.role: Provides proto-audit, the netlink layout oracle.
known_bugs_at_this_rev: samples/proto_audit/src/extractors/xtcp2.rs:143 extract_size_const() builds the pattern `{struct}SizeCst`, but xtcp2 spells these `TCPInfo7_0_3_SizeCst` with an underscore, so no versioned size constant is ever matched and the struct size is inferred from field offsets. Visible as `extract --source xtcp2 --proto NL_Diag_TCPInfo` reporting min_header_bytes 283 rather than 280: 283 is the end of the last unpacked Go field, not the size of the wire struct. Harmless for the oracle, which compares by bit offset and treats min_header_bytes as a minimum.
fixed_at_this_rev: The `.xtcp2("TCPInfo6_10_3")` registry pin in samples/proto_audit/src/name_mapping/table.rs, which made the 11 Accurate ECN fields read as missing from xtcp2. Fixed to `.xtcp2("TCPInfo")` by https://github.com/randomizedcoder/xdp2/pull/11, merged 2026-09-26 as this rev, so resolve_alias() now follows `type TCPInfo TCPInfo7_0_3`. MEASURED across the bump: NL_Diag_TCPInfo goes 76/54/3/8/11 to 80/61/3/16/0 (total/agree/type_differ/mismatch/missing). Note that the fix was NOT 11 missing becoming 11 agreements: the 7 plain __u32 counters became agreements and need no allowlist entry, while the other 4 are members of the packed __u32 at [276:280] and surfaced as 4 kind=split PAIRS - 8 new entries, one per side, at offsets 2208/2210/2212/2216 (kernel, tcpi_*) and 2208/2216/2224/2232 (xtcp2, bare names). Allowlist went 22 -> 19. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo in nix/checks/proto-audit-netlink-allowlist.json.
xdp2.on_bump: Re-run `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.proto-audit-netlink` and read $out/unallowlisted.json before anything else. A proto-audit bump can change what the oracle reports, so it should land on its own rather than inside unrelated work.
xdp2.recheck_on_bump: Rebuild .#checks.x86_64-linux.proto-audit-netlink and read $out/unallowlisted-gated.json, not $out/unallowlisted.json. NL_Diag_TCPInfo is a gated protocol, so a delta there fails the build; the ~179 advisory deltas on the other protocols are expected and do not.

xdp2-embedded-xtcp2.verify_via: grep xtcp2Rev in the xdp2 flake input's source tree
xdp2-embedded-xtcp2.consumed_by: proto-audit itself, whenever --xtcp2-src is NOT overridden
xdp2-embedded-xtcp2.stale_note: Dated 2025-04-19 and 732 commits behind xtcp2 main as of 2026-09-26 — it predates essentially all of the netlink coverage work, including the 7 kernel-versioned TCPInfo variants and the AccECN trailer. Auditing it would re-report the very gap that work closed. This is EXPECTED to be stale and is not a bug to fix here: the fix is that every xtcp2-side proto-audit invocation overrides the path. The runner still reports it so the number cannot quietly grow into something worse without anyone noticing, and so that bumping it upstream is an informed choice rather than a surprise.

_comment_package_pins: A SECOND KIND OF PIN, in its own key because it is not a git rev.
Everything under `pins` is a branch tip: a repo, a branch and a 40-hex
rev, which `nix run .#check-upstream-pins` can compare against
`git ls-remote`. The entries below pin a NIXPKGS PACKAGE VERSION instead.
There is no ref to ls-remote and no rev to compare, so the networked
runner skips this key entirely and says so. The version is in the store
at eval time, which for once makes the hermetic half of the guard the
stronger one: nix/checks/upstream-pins.nix reads pkgs.iproute2.version
directly and so cannot be out of date with the build it runs in.
WHY IT IS PINNED AT ALL. The goip netlink-parity work compares the bytes
goip puts on the wire against the bytes a specific `ip` was recorded
emitting, and request bytes are a function of the iproute2 SOURCE rather
than of the kernel. A bare `ip link show` request is 40 bytes carrying
IFLA_EXT_MASK = 0x09 because iproute2 7.1.0's iplink_filter_req() sets
RTEXT_FILTER_VF and RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS; a release that changed that
would move the expected bytes without a line of this repo changing.
Unpinned, a routine nixpkgs bump fails the parity gate for a reason that
has nothing to do with goip - the risk the goip plan records as Risk 3,
and the reason parity must not gate until this entry exists.
Refresh `version` here when nixpkgs moves, then re-run
`sudo nix run .#capture-netlink-fixtures` and diff the new ip_* sidecars
before trusting any request-byte expectation.

iproute2.declared_in: the nixpkgs flake input; not overridden anywhere in this repo
iproute2.verify_via: nix/checks/upstream-pins.nix, which compares this against pkgs.iproute2.version at eval time
iproute2.role: The netlink parity target. goip's request bytes are compared against what this `ip` was recorded emitting, and this `ip`'s rendering is the source of truth behind every ip_* sidecar under pkg/xtcpnl/testdata/<kernel>/.
iproute2.consumed_by: nix/capture-netlink-fixtures.nix (both the pcaps and the ip_* sidecars), internal/goip's request and rendering tables, pkg/nlparity
iproute2.recorded_in_fixtures: pkg/xtcpnl/testdata/<kernel>/ip_version, written by `ip -V`. That sidecar is the per-capture record and this entry is the build-time assertion; the two are expected to agree, and a capture whose ip_version disagrees with this pin was taken with a different ip than the one the checks run against.
known_agreements: IFLA_EXT_MASK = 0x09 on a bare `ip link show`, verified on the 7.1.0 wire AND in the 7.2.0 source. filter.vfinfo is set unconditionally at ip/ipaddress.c:2153, shared by `link show` and `addr show`, and iplink_filter_req() at :2019-2026 ors in RTEXT_FILTER_VF plus RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS when !show_stats. So there is no ext-mask version skew to allowlist, which is what made the request encoder worth writing before cmd/goip existed. The other arm of the same `if` is now measured too: `ip -s link show` sends 0x01, confirmed by netlink_route_getlink_stats.pcap, which is the same 40-byte datagram with RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS cleared and is asserted directly in pkg/xtcpnl's TestLinkStatsRequestExtMask.
known_divergences_from_7_2_0: THREE commits move IFLA_EXT_MASK, and they hit the two ll_map loci differently - measured on the pinned wire, not read off the diffstat. ll_link_get (lib/ll_map.c:276) is already RTEXT_FILTER_VF|RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS = 0x09 at 7.1.0, confirmed by netlink_route_getlink_dev.pcap, so only de91e928 touches it: 0x09 -> 0x109. ll_init_map is NOT 0x09 at 7.1.0 - it calls rtnl_linkdump_req(rth, AF_UNSPEC), which forwards RTEXT_FILTER_VF alone, and netlink_route_getneigh.pcap records 01000000 on the wire. 7bd7f335 (2026-04-28) takes it 0x01 -> 0x09 and de91e928 (2026-05-20) takes it 0x09 -> 0x109. Both loci have version-skew allowlist entries in pkg/nlparity/goip-parity-allowlist.json.

faceb326 has TWO loci, not one, and that was measured rather than read off the diffstat. The small half is the `if (qlen)` guard in print_queuelen, which runs the other way round from the obvious reading: 7.1.0 SUPPRESSES `qlen 0` and a post-faceb326 release prints it, because the commit replaced `if (qlen) print_int(...)` with an unconditional print_uint(...). The large half is a SIOCGIFTXQLEN ioctl fallback for when IFLA_TXQLEN is absent from the reply - unreachable on any command answered by rtnl_dump_ifinfo, but live on `ip -6 addr show`, whose link dump is answered by inet6_dump_ifinfo and carries no IFLA_TXQLEN at all. Flipping the render-time qlen knob cannot restore an absent attribute, which is the proof that the two loci are independent and that one allowlist entry would not cover both.
iproute2.on_bump: Re-read the two known_divergences entries first: they are stated against 7.1.0, and a bump can resolve them, move them, or add to them. Then regenerate the fixtures and diff the ip_* sidecars before touching any Go expectation, because a rendering change shifts the line numbers those expectations cite.
